question: Should OpenClaw permanently define QA coverage as one globally unique exact `<surface-id>.<feature-id>` per taxonomy feature and define `smoke-ci` only by categories evidenced by its fixed scenario plan?
rationale: This is an internal QA governance and reporting-policy choice, not a mechanical correctness question: it changes how coverage completeness and CI-profile eligibility are interpreted across the taxonomy.

options.title: Approve the canonical QA contract
options.body: Accept atomic exact IDs and the fixed-plan definition of `smoke-ci`, then merge once required exact-head checks are green.

options.title: Preserve broader smoke semantics
options.body: Keep a broader `smoke-ci` category contract and request a revised selector/report design that distinguishes fixed-plan execution from broader eligibility.

options.title: Split the policy decision
options.body: Land only the validation and attribution cleanup after separating any disputed taxonomy or smoke-profile remapping into a smaller follow-up.

recommendation.title: Approve the canonical QA contract
recommendation.body: Accept atomic exact IDs and the fixed-plan definition of `smoke-ci`, then merge once required exact-head checks are green.

likelyOwner.reason: The current member-authored branch and its QA contract rationale provide the closest available ownership signal for this decision.
